newsitem.title: UK: Russia's Dubinin sees two pct 1997 GDP grwoth.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Dubinin sees two pct 1997 GDP grwoth.

text.p: Russian central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Tuesday he was conservatively estimating GDP growth of two percent for 1997.
"This is a very conservative estimate," he told a conference in London.
Dubinin's comments followed forecasts on Saturday by opposition politician Grigory Yavlinksy that the economy would contract by between 2.0 and 2.5 percent this year.

Dubinin told Reuters following the address: "In the past few years Yavlinsky has predicted higher inflation and less economic growth than we have seen in reality...He is speaking not as an economist but as a politician".
According to official statistics, Russian GDP contracted by six percent in 1996.
